children.lean_statement: ∀ m : ℕ, 1 ≤ m → ∀ F : (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m)) → (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m)), ContDiff ℝ 1 F → ∀ X : Fin m → (Matrix (Fin m) (Fin m) ℝ), (∀ r, (X r).IsHermitian) → Finset.sum Finset.univ (fun r : Fin m => X r * X r) = (1 : (Matrix (Fin m) (Fin m) ℝ)) → (∀ x v i, (fderiv ℝ F x v) i = Finset.sum Finset.univ (fun j : Fin m => (cfc (fun t : ℝ => ProbabilityTheory.gaussianPDFReal 0 1 t / ProbabilityTheory.cdf (ProbabilityTheory.gaussianReal 0 1) (-t)) (Finset.sum Finset.univ (fun r : Fin m => x r • X r))) i j * v j)) → ∃ Q : (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m)) ≃ₗᵢ[ℝ] (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m)), ∃ a : (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m)), (∀ x : (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m)), ∀ i : Fin m, (Q.symm (F (Q x) - a)) i = -Real.log (ProbabilityTheory.cdf (ProbabilityTheory.gaussianReal 0 1) (-x i)))
children.nl_statement: Lemma 6.1 through its rigid-map formula: the prescribed Gaussian-hazard Jacobian of a linear Hermitian field with square-sum identity forces an orthogonal coordinatewise -log Gaussian-survival representation, with all coordinate signs absorbed into the orthogonal map.
children.role_in_glue: Provides the orthogonal equivalence Q, translation a, and pointwise coordinate formula to which the independent Gaussian-law child applies.

children.nl_statement: Last paragraph of Lemma 6.1: an orthogonally conjugated coordinatewise -log Gaussian-survival map has the explicit affine exponential-product density, and when centered its full raw second-moment matrix equals I.
children.role_in_glue: Applied to Q and a from normal_form, proves the density using L=Q.toLinearEquiv and the covariance conjunct of o011.

notes: Two independent parts of the supplied paper Lemma 6.1. The normal-form child has no moment or centering hypotheses; the Gaussian-law child has no Jacobian, coefficient, or functional-calculus hypotheses. Existing original-tree matrix algebra/primitive helpers can be reused in the first child once available; no such unaccepted theorem is assumed in the glue. PROOF.md spells out analytic compatibility, sign absorption, scalar probability integral transform, affine density, and full covariance.
